hypothesis: A weekly long/flat trend portfolio may retain an economic edge after costs; Timestral forecasts squared-return risk rather than direction and must be compared with the same strategy using EWMA risk.

model.target: log(daily close-to-close return squared + 1e-8), two jointly forecast variates
model.variance_rule: sum(exp(median forecast days 2..8)), no subtracting epsilon (conservative floor)

rules.schedule: Monday 00 UTC uses closed days through Sunday; weights executed Tuesday open, held to following Tuesday open; exclude trades whose exit is at/after source end
rules.trend: positive trailing 126 daily close-to-close log return; otherwise asset weight zero
rules.weights: per asset min(0.5,0.5*target_vol/sqrt(calibrated_weekly_variance*365/7)); no leverage; remainder cash earns zero
rules.calibration: mean(realized/predicted weekly variance) over latest 52 fully matured weekly forecasts per asset and risk method; exclude outcome_end > current Monday anchor; minimum 26 observations
comparators: same trend rule with EWMA risk, 20-day half-life over last 256 daily squared log returns
same trend rule with fixed 0.5 asset weights
continuous equal initial allocation buy-and-hold, no rebalancing
rules.accounting: self-financing cash/units portfolio; transaction costs only on changed holdings; solve post-cost target NAV; unwind all holdings at last exit; allow fractional quantities; no fills claim

gate: historical candidate only: net CAGR >5%, weekly net mean lower 99% stationary-block CI >0, exit-marked max drawdown <=25%; Timestral incremental value requires positive lower 99% CI on paired weekly utility gain over EWMA, utility=r-3*r*r/2. No prospective success claim.

trial_count.old_trials: unknown; extensive prior research; no global significance claim

protected_data: Do not request source dates >=2026-08-01; do not read original protected artifacts.
limitations: Historical zero-shot pretraining overlap cannot be ruled out
